title: Music Songs search and Load more behave cleanly at the edges (RF-132 review follow-ups)
acceptance: Clearing and retyping several searches within a minute does not end in "Couldn't load more songs" from the provider-likes limiter: search autoload keeps a client-side per-minute budget or its own limiter.
Whitespace-only edits do not start a new search (the trimmed query is compared).
An autoload tick that sends no request does not count against the 5-request budget, and a Keep loading grant does not reset during its round.
After an account switch, the previous account's songs are hidden until the new account's first page arrives.
Retyping a query after clearing it does not briefly show a stale Apple search result or failure.
The owner decides whether the first search's 1,000-song bound counts songs already loaded (today it does, matching the 2026-10-29 ruling) or is relative.
Each changed behavior has a Dashboard or music-library test.

evidence.summary: Final review of #665 on 42da99c: no significant findings; items 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 logged for Backlog.
Final review of #665 on 0a66217: logged items 4 (re-search on whitespace-only edits) and 5 (Keep loading counts a request that never fires and can reset during a round).
Owner pre-approved RF-152 items 1-5 and 7 for the 2026-11-05 unattended Neo session, item 1 client-side only; item 6 stays an owner decision.

Neo local: four new RF-152 tests and the extended previous-account test all failed with the Dashboard change reverted (15 autoload requests against at most 10 per minute; 2 Apple searches for a whitespace edit; stale Apple result shown; 6 requests after Keep loading taps in a running round; old account songs visible) and pass with it. music-library songSearchAutoLoadDelay tests added. Dashboard.test.tsx and music-library.test.ts: 247 passed before the new tests. A fresh-context review found the per-minute budget was per service while the server limit is per user; it is now one budget across services, and a new cross-service test failed on the earlier commit (15 requests against at most 10) and passes now. A third review found the budget reset when leaving Music (now held by Dashboard; a new test failed with 15 requests and passes) and that a disconnect then reconnect as another account could keep the old songs (the disconnect path now clears them). A fourth review found the Apple library search result was not tied to the account (another account's matches could stay after a switch while the query was typed): the result now carries likesConnectionKey and only a result for the current connection shows (a re-authorization that keeps the same connection row is not detected; RF-202); the disconnect clear also drops the cursor. That account-switch path has no component test yet (RF-202).
RF-152 items 1-5 and 7 PR, opened under unattended pre-approval issue #730 after four fresh-context /code-review high passes (significant findings fixed; follow-ups in RF-202).

Owner decision on item 6 (live Neo session, 2026-11-05): the first search's 1,000-song bound keeps counting songs already loaded, as main does and as the 2026-10-29 ruling set; it is not made relative. No code change is needed.

resolution: Items 1-5 and 7 shipped in #735 (one client-side autoload budget of 10 a minute across services, trimmed-query compare, budget counts only sent requests, account-switch and disconnect clear old songs, Apple search result tied to its connection, tests). Item 6: the owner kept the 1,000-song bound counting songs already loaded, which is main's existing behavior. Follow-ups in RF-202.
